task: Stage 1 MR1 workforce entrypoint convergence: make the active platform, customer-account bridge, template-preview and workforce invitation surfaces consume the already-verified canonical Workforce Auth Core without changing identity primitives, role/tenant authority, middleware or parked AAL2 enforcement.

exceptions.reason: Exact-fingerprint review only: the customer account layout intentionally continues to render StorefrontAccountShell for shopper account presentation. The changed workforce-only template preview login removed that shell because it now delegates immediately to canonical workforce authentication; the customer layout is not a workforce authentication or authorization consumer.

Exact-fingerprint review only: the closing StorefrontAccountShell expression belongs to the unchanged shopper account layout. It is intentionally independent from the workforce-only preview-login route and does not consume or override workforce login, role, tenant or MFA authority.

assuranceCeiling.rationale: The canonical Workforce Auth Core is already exact-head VERIFIED on main. This transaction changes only active ADMIN, BUILDER and STOREFRONT entrypoint/delegator surfaces so they consume that authority. A defect could preserve an alternate privileged password surface, route preview users through shopper authentication, misroute workforce invitations, or reopen the high-risk auth release scope.

acceptanceCriteria: The active /platform page no longer imports or renders legacy PlatformAuthForm; existing workforce users delegate to canonical workforce login and owner activation consumes the verified auth-owned activation primitive.
The template-preview login route no longer renders customer AuthForm or StorefrontAccountShell; it delegates to canonical workforce login with the exact sanitized preview target.

Explicit /fiokom workforce intent bridges allowed admin and exact template-preview targets through the shared workforce return-target helper before storefront instance resolution; ordinary shopper sign-in remains unchanged.
Platform-created workforce invitations redirect to the verified workforce-owned credential completion route instead of shopper /fiokom onboarding.
All four active delegates consume the merged Workforce Auth Core from main; no Auth Core implementation file is modified in this transaction.
No role, tenant, middleware authorization authority or AAL2 enforcement is added, weakened or activated.

The delegator release consumes the current main Workforce Auth contract including prepared/enforced MFA activation semantics; it does not configure WORKFORCE_MFA_MODE, alter target factor policy, or activate server-side AAL2 enforcement.
invariants: Supabase Auth remains the only session/password/MFA authority.
The merged Workforce Auth Core on main is read-only in this release unit.
Server-owned platform operator, role and tenant authorities remain unchanged.
Customer AuthForm remains shopper-owned and is not used by workforce-only preview or invitation flows.
The release transaction contains no substantive src/lib/auth or src/app/api/auth implementation edits.
WORKFORCE_MFA_MODE remains server-owned Auth Core configuration inherited from main; this delegator transaction must not set, expose publicly, or override it.

failureModes: The platform page keeps PlatformAuthForm or another direct privileged signInWithPassword path.
The template-preview login still renders customer AuthForm/StorefrontAccountShell rather than delegating to workforce login.
The /fiokom workforce bridge only handles /admin and loses the exact preview return target supported by the verified Auth Core.
A platform invitation still redirects to shopper /fiokom invite UX instead of workforce credential completion.
A delegator reimplements redirect allowlisting locally and diverges from the shared fail-closed workforce helper.
The change edits Auth Core, require-admin, middleware or tenant resolution and accidentally reopens authority/AAL2 semantics.
The release reintroduces the combined-branch Release Risk Budget failure by mixing substantive auth implementation with ADMIN/BUILDER/STOREFRONT delegates.
edgeCases: Existing shopper flows through /fiokom remain shopper-owned unless reason=login and the normalized target is workforce-allowed.
Exact /storefront-template-preview with query parameters survives the bridge; preview-login loops and external targets remain rejected by the merged helper.
An already authenticated user opening preview login still traverses canonical workforce login/context processing rather than bypassing it.
First-owner activation continues through the merged auth-owned activation component and then canonical workforce login.
Invite redirects preserve next=/admin in encoded form for credential completion.
Legacy PlatformAuthForm may remain as dead source but must have zero active App Router references.

alternatives.summary: Merge the original combined Auth Core plus delegator branch.
alternatives.reason: That transaction already proved 10/5 Release Risk Budget and would discard the successful isolation of Auth Core.

alternatives.summary: Keep route-local login/redirect logic in platform, account and preview surfaces.
alternatives.reason: That preserves parallel privileged entry authorities and allows drift from the verified Workforce Auth Core.

alternatives.summary: Change only ADMIN, BUILDER and STOREFRONT callers so they consume the already-verified Workforce Auth Core.
alternatives.reason: This completes convergence without reopening high-risk identity implementation and keeps release scope dependency-closed.

specialistReviews.finding: ADMIN, BUILDER and STOREFRONT presentation surfaces must consume DOMAIN-IDENTITY contracts rather than own privileged authentication policy.
specialistReviews.resolution: The four active surfaces become thin delegators; merged Auth Core files remain read-only.

specialistReviews.finding: Delegation is unsafe if any surface retains customer AuthForm/direct password behavior or locally broadens return-target acceptance.
specialistReviews.resolution: Source-contract regressions require zero active PlatformAuthForm reference, no preview customer AuthForm, workforce-owned invite completion and shared return-target consumption.

specialistReviews.finding: The original combined change exceeded Release Risk Budget because Auth Core and three presentation/operations subsystems shipped together.
specialistReviews.resolution: Auth Core was merged separately in PR #911; this second transaction contains only delegator callers and neutral proof files.

challenge.scenario: A platform operator opens /platform with an existing workforce account.
challenge.finding: Keeping PlatformAuthForm would preserve a parallel direct-password privileged entrypoint.
challenge.resolution: The page imports workforceLoginHref and PlatformActivationForm only; active App Router modules have zero PlatformAuthForm references.

challenge.scenario: An unauthenticated operator opens a template preview deep link.
challenge.finding: Rendering customer AuthForm would mix shopper and workforce UX.
challenge.resolution: Preview login validates the preview request and redirects to canonical workforce login with the sanitized preview target.

challenge.scenario: A merchant owner/admin accepts a platform-generated invitation.
challenge.finding: Redirecting to /fiokom would mix workforce credential establishment with shopper onboarding.
challenge.resolution: Invitation redirect targets /api/auth/workforce-credential?flow=invite and then the merged Auth Core owns credential completion.

challenge.scenario: A legacy workforce bridge enters through /fiokom with a preview target rather than /admin.
challenge.finding: An admin-only local condition would drop a legitimate exact preview target or diverge from canonical allowlisting.
challenge.resolution: The bridge calls normalizeWorkforceReturnTarget and workforceLoginHref before storefront instance resolution.

challenge.scenario: A caller supplies an unsafe or looping next target.
challenge.finding: Route-local prefix logic could broaden the safe set.
challenge.resolution: Delegators do not implement a second allowlist; they consume the exact merged auth-owned helper, whose regression remains in the proof set.

challenge.scenario: Entrypoint convergence is mistaken for authorization/MFA enforcement.
challenge.finding: Editing requireAdmin, middleware or tenant resolution would alter authority before final audit.
challenge.resolution: Those files remain impacted-read-only and #858 stays parked.

challenge.scenario: The second release accidentally includes substantive Auth Core edits.
challenge.finding: That would recreate the Release Risk Budget violation already proven on the combined branch.
challenge.resolution: Plan envelope excludes auth implementation files and Release Risk Budget is a required CAP-RELEASE proof.

proofPlan: Run Plan Before Code on this exact plan-only head before any delegate implementation edit.
Apply only the four active delegator changes and the seven targeted regression-test changes from the preserved combined reference branch.
Run Edit-Time / Reference Sync and Incremental Known Failure Replay on the implementation head.
Require Release Risk Budget PASS without substantive Auth Core scope.
Run full Quality Tests, TypeScript and Production Build.
Require exact-head Completion Truth VERIFIED and lifecycle closure before merge.
Require the exact-head E13/Template Factory browser proof to traverse canonical workforce entry under prepared MFA activation and retain its existing fail-closed side-effect assertions.

requirements.requirement: Active platform, account-bridge, template-preview and workforce-invitation entrypoints consume the verified canonical Workforce Auth Core while shopper authentication, server RBAC/tenant authority and parked AAL2 enforcement remain separate and unchanged.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: Platform and Builder preview surfaces must not retain a separate privileged signInWithPassword/customer AuthForm path.
Workforce invitation/login continuation must not require shopper AuthForm semantics.
Delegators must consume the canonical workforce return-target authority rather than broadening or duplicating it.
This release must not merge, weaken or activate the parked AAL2 authorization enforcement.

requirements.requirement: The second convergence release remains isolated from substantive Auth Core implementation and satisfies the canonical Release Risk Budget.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: The delegator release must not include substantive Auth Core implementation changes or recreate the original mixed high-risk release.

notes: Auth Core was isolated and merged in PR #911. E13 proof-harness compatibility was then merged to main, and PR #922 added the verified server-owned WORKFORCE_MFA_MODE prepared/enforced activation control at main b2d5d4f4b3a0831aa2879bdb9bf6f14b55361c46. This reconstructed second transaction reapplies only the four ADMIN/BUILDER/STOREFRONT delegator changes plus their seven targeted regressions on top of that verified main. MFA target policy remains intact; default interactive activation remains prepared. PR #858 stays parked and AAL2 server enforcement stays inactive. The preserved combined reference branch must not be merged.
